# ObserveCo

> ObserveCo is a differentiation strategy consultancy in Singapore. It studies a small
> business's real competitive set and hands the owner the one differentiator most likely
> to make customers choose them. Founded by Sean Foo, author of two books on the subject,
> both with National Library Board (NLB) Singapore ISBNs. Works with Singapore SMEs.
> Everything below is public and stable; last reviewed 2026-10-20.

## What ObserveCo sells

- **The Differentiation Strategy** — from S$500, one engagement. Delivered in 3–7 days from a
  30-minute call. Includes the real competitive set, every viable differentiator evaluated
  against the client's own market, the open position and the traps, a positioning statement,
  and a 90-day roadmap. Guarantee: if ObserveCo does not identify the client's best
  differentiator, the client does not pay.
- **Differentiation Watch** — S$300–400 per quarter. Quarterly re-run of the competitive
  analysis, new-entrant alerts, refreshed recommendation.

## The method

Four steps: Observe → Uncover → Differentiate → Be Chosen. The analysis is assisted by AI;
a named person reviews, decides, and owns every recommendation. The underlying framework
follows the positioning method of Al Ries, Jack Trout and Gu Junhui, applied to live
Singapore markets rather than imported theory.

## The founder

- Sean Foo — founder. 15 years in consulting, 18 in startups. Previously Stuart Wright Well
  Consultancy (offshore complex wells, Australia), AlgoMerchant (Singapore's first AI
  robo-investing solution), Aurora Energy Research (European power analytics).
- Books: *Small Island, Crowded Market* (ISBN 978-981-94-7829-3) and
  *How a Small Business Gets Chosen* (ISBN 978-981-94-7828-6). Published September 2026.
  NLB Singapore ISBNs. DRM-free ebooks via Bookshop.org.

## Figures ObserveCo cites, with sources

- ~50% of new Singapore businesses do not survive five years — ACRA
- 213 new business registrations per day — ACRA, 2025
- 55% of Singapore SME decision-makers cite getting/keeping customers as a top concern — QBE 2025 (n=600)
- 39% → 50% of Singapore SMEs citing increasing competition, 2024→2025 — QBE 2025
- 36% cite market competition as their number one concern — OCBC 4Q2025
- 25,000 enterprises a year receive free 1-to-1 advice from Enterprise Singapore SME Centres

These are third-party statistics, cited to their publishers. They are not ObserveCo estimates.

  Different organisations, different subject matter, same name string.
